eyebrow: SQL for Oracle Financials · Chapter Five
subtitle: Lesson 22 · Investigating Financial Data

eyebrow: Wrong on its own, no 2nd table needed
caption: Zero or negative invoice amounts where none were expected — a classic data-entry red flag.

code:
SELECT i.invoice_num, i.invoice_amount, SUM(ip.amount) AS total_paid
FROM ap_invoices_all i
INNER JOIN ap_invoice_payments_all ip ON ip.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
GROUP BY i.invoice_num, i.invoice_amount
HAVING SUM(ip.amount) > i.invoice_amount;
caption: HAVING > (not <> 0) — overpayment is the operationally urgent direction to catch.

code:
SELECT 'Negative/Zero Amount' AS exception_type, invoice_num, invoice_amount
FROM ap_invoices_all WHERE invoice_amount <= 0
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Overpaid', i.invoice_num, i.invoice_amount
FROM ap_invoices_all i
INNER JOIN ap_invoice_payments_all ip ON ip.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
GROUP BY i.invoice_num, i.invoice_amount
HAVING SUM(ip.amount) > i.invoice_amount;
caption: UNION ALL combines independent exception checks, each labeled by exception_type.
